samples.text:
The table show information about the underground railway systems in six different cities, including the year each one was opened, the length of the route and how many passengers use it every year.

Firstly, the oldest system is in Riverton, which opened in 1890, and it is also the longest with 402 km of route. Castelle opened in 1902 and has 225 km, but it carries the most passengers, about 1,450 million per year. Riverton is in second place with 1,210 million passengers. Norwick system was opened in 1935 and it have 118 km and 520 million passengers.

Also, the newer systems are smaller in general. Ashbury opened in 1967 and it has only 96 km and 310 million passengers. Port Maren is quite new, it opened in 2001, but it is bigger than Norwick and Ashbury with 184 km and 870 million passengers. The newest one is Delmont in 2014 and it is the smallest in the both length and passengers, with 62 km and 145 million.

Overall, the older underground systems are usually longer and busier than the newer ones, although Port Maren is a exception.
samples.why: Key features covered with accurate figures · overview present but placed at the end · mechanical linking (Firstly, Also) · adequate vocabulary · several agreement and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table compares six cities' underground railway networks in terms of when they opened, how long their routes are and how many passengers they carry annually.

Overall, the older systems tend to be both more extensive and more heavily used, while the most recently built networks are generally smaller. Castelle and Riverton stand out as by far the busiest systems.

Riverton has the oldest network, dating from 1890, and it is also the longest at 402 km. However, it is Castelle, opened twelve years later in 1902, that carries the highest number of passengers, with 1,450 million a year compared with Riverton's 1,210 million, despite having a route of only 225 km. Norwick, which opened in 1935, has a much shorter network of 118 km and serves 520 million passengers.

Of the later systems, Port Maren, opened in 2001, is the most significant, with 184 km of route and 870 million passengers, which is more than Norwick and Ashbury. Ashbury's system, built in 1967, is only 96 km long and is used by 310 million people each year. Finally, Delmont has the newest and smallest network, having opened in 2014 with just 62 km and 145 million passengers annually.
samples.why: Clear overview of the age–size pattern · key features highlighted and compared · logical grouping by period · good range of linking and some less common vocabulary · one or two minor imprecisions.

samples.text:
The table provides details of the underground railway networks in six cities, specifically their opening dates, route lengths and annual passenger numbers.

In general, there is a broad correlation between age and scale: the earliest networks are the most extensive and carry the greatest numbers of passengers, whereas those opened more recently are considerably smaller. The one notable exception to this pattern is Port Maren.

The two oldest systems clearly dominate. Riverton's network, opened in 1890, is the longest by a wide margin at 402 km, almost twice the length of Castelle's 225 km. Nevertheless, Castelle, which dates from 1902, is the busiest, handling 1,450 million passengers a year against Riverton's 1,210 million. Norwick (1935) and Ashbury (1967) operate far more modest systems of 118 km and 96 km respectively, with annual ridership of 520 million and 310 million.

Port Maren breaks the trend. Although it did not open until 2001, its network of 184 km is the third longest, and it carries 870 million passengers annually, well ahead of both Norwick and Ashbury. Delmont, by contrast, has the youngest and smallest system: opened in 2014, it covers just 62 km and serves 145 million passengers, exactly a tenth of Castelle's total.
samples.why: Well-placed overview identifying the overall correlation and its exception · figures selected skilfully for comparison · cohesion managed effortlessly · precise, natural vocabulary · wide range of structures, virtually error-free.
